title: Human Digestive System
description: An introduction to the organs and processes involved in human digestion.
transcript: Digestion begins in the mouth. Teeth break food into smaller pieces, and saliva moistens the food. The tongue helps form food into a bolus that can be swallowed. The bolus moves through the esophagus to the stomach. Muscles in the stomach mix food with gastric juices, producing a semi-liquid mixture. This mixture passes into the small intestine. In the small intestine, digestive juices continue breaking food down, and nutrients pass through the intestinal wall into the bloodstream. Material that is not absorbed moves into the large intestine, where water is absorbed. The remaining waste is stored in the rectum until it leaves the body through the anus.
study_material: The digestive system processes food so the body can absorb nutrients and water. The main pathway is mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, and anus. Digestion includes mechanical breakdown, such as chewing and stomach mixing, and chemical breakdown by digestive juices. Most nutrient absorption takes place in the small intestine. The large intestine absorbs water from the remaining material. The rectum stores waste before it is eliminated.
